records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר דָּוִ֤יד הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ לְכָל־הַקָּהָ֔ל שְׁלֹמֹ֨ה בְנִ֥י אֶחָ֛ד בָּֽחַר־בּ֥וֹ אֱלֹהִ֖ים נַ֣עַר וָרָ֑ךְ וְהַמְּלָאכָ֣ה גְדוֹלָ֔ה כִּ֣י לֹ֤א לְאָדָם֙ הַבִּירָ֔ה כִּ֖י לַיהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהִֽים׃
records.gloss: And said David the king to all the assembly, Solomon my son, one [whom] has chosen him God, [is] young and tender, and the work [is] great, for not for man [is] the palace, but for Yahweh God.
pieces: King David then spoke to the whole assembly: "God has chosen my son Solomon alone, but he is young and inexperienced, and the task is great, because this palace is not for {{gender:a human being|man}} but for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God.

L.1: And David the king said to all the assembly, "Solomon my son, the one whom God has chosen, [is] young and tender, and the work [is] great, for the palace [is] not for {{gender:a human|man}} but for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God.

R.1: Then King David said to all the people gathered there, "God has chosen my son Solomon, and only him. But Solomon is young and has little experience, and the work is great. This palace is not for {{gender:a human being|a man}}. It is for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God.

decisions.choice: palace: a great fortified royal building, here the temple
decisions.reason: The word names a citadel or fortified palace. It is used of the royal citadel at Susa (Nehemiah 1:1; Esther 1:2) and of the fortress beside the temple (Nehemiah 2:8). Calling the temple by this word sets the house of Yahweh beside a king's palace: it is a royal residence, but its king is God, not a human ruler. The word comes again in verse 19.

decisions.choice: the one whom God has chosen: the one son chosen
decisions.reason: The word 'one' stresses that of David's many sons (3:1-9) God chose Solomon alone to sit on the throne and build the house (28:5-6).

decisions.choice: young and tender: young and inexperienced
decisions.reason: David said the same in 22:5. The pair describes youth without experience, not weakness of body; Solomon calls himself 'a young boy' who does not know how to lead in 1 Kings 3:7.

decisions.choice: a human / a human being, with 'man' as the alternative
decisions.reason: The word means a human being in general, set against God, so the inclusive form is the default.

records.heading: Gifts for the temple

records.source: וּֽכְכָל־כֹּחִ֞י הֲכִינ֣וֹתִי לְבֵית־אֱלֹהַ֗י הַזָּהָ֣ב׀לַ֠זָּהָב וְהַכֶּ֨סֶף לַכֶּ֜סֶף וְהַנְּחֹ֣שֶׁת לַנְּחֹ֗שֶׁת הַבַּרְזֶל֙ לַבַּרְזֶ֔ל וְהָעֵצִ֖ים לָעֵצִ֑ים אַבְנֵי־שֹׁ֨הַם וּמִלּוּאִ֜ים אַבְנֵי־פ֣וּךְ וְרִקְמָ֗ה וְכֹ֨ל אֶ֧בֶן יְקָרָ֛ה וְאַבְנֵי־שַׁ֖יִשׁ לָרֹֽב׃
records.gloss: And with all my strength I have prepared for [the] house of my God the gold for the gold and the silver for the silver and the bronze for the bronze, the iron for the iron, and the wood for the wood, stones of onyx and settings, stones of antimony and varied color, and every stone precious, and stones of alabaster in abundance.
pieces: With all my strength I have provided for the house of my God: gold for the things of gold and silver for the things of silver, bronze and iron for what is to be made of them, and timber for the woodwork, along with onyx stones and stones for setting, dark antimony stones and stones of many colors, every kind of precious stone, and alabaster in great quantity.

L.2: And with all my strength I have prepared for the house of my God the gold for the [things of] gold, and the silver for the [things of] silver, and the bronze for the [things of] bronze, the iron for the [things of] iron, and the wood for the [things of] wood, onyx stones and [stones for] settings, stones of antimony and of varied colors, and every [kind of] precious stone, and alabaster stones in abundance.

R.2: I have worked as hard as I could to get things ready for the house of my God. I have gathered gold and silver, bronze and iron, and timber, each for the objects to be made from it. I have also gathered onyx and other stones to be set in place, dark stones, stones of many colors, all kinds of valuable jewels, and a great amount of fine white stone.

decisions.choice: the gold for the gold: the material for each kind of object
decisions.reason: The repeated pairs mean the gold for what was to be made of gold, the silver for what was to be made of silver, and so on, as in the list of 28:14-18.

decisions.choice: onyx stones and stones for setting
decisions.reason: The same pair appears among the gifts for the tabernacle (Exodus 25:7; 35:9). The first is a precious stone often taken as onyx or carnelian; the second means stones to be mounted, as in the high priest's breastpiece (Exodus 28:17).

decisions.choice: antimony: dark stones
decisions.reason: The word elsewhere names the black eye paint made from antimony (2 Kings 9:30), and in Isaiah 54:11 God sets Jerusalem's stones 'in antimony'. Here it may mean dark stones, or a dark material in which other stones were set.

decisions.choice: alabaster: a fine white stone
decisions.reason: The word appears only here in this form; a closely related word names white stone in Esther 1:6. It is a fine white stone, alabaster or marble.

decisions.choice: gold for the things of gold / gold for the gold objects
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable spell out what the bare pairs mean the first time, then shorten them as the list goes on.

records.source: וְע֗וֹד בִּרְצוֹתִי֙ בְּבֵ֣ית אֱלֹהַ֔י יֶשׁ־לִ֥י סְגֻלָּ֖ה זָהָ֣ב וָכָ֑סֶף נָתַ֤תִּי לְבֵית־אֱלֹהַי֙ לְמַ֔עְלָה מִכָּל־הֲכִינ֖וֹתִי לְבֵ֥ית הַקֹּֽדֶשׁ׃
records.gloss: And moreover, in my delighting in [the] house of my God, there is to me a treasure, gold and silver; I give [it] for [the] house of my God, upward above all [that] I have prepared for [the] house of the holiness:
pieces: Moreover, because I delight in the house of my God, I am giving my own treasure of gold and silver to the house of my God, over and above everything I have provided for the holy house:

L.3: And moreover, in my delight in the house of my God, there is to me a treasured possession of gold and silver; I give [it] to the house of my God, over and above all that I have prepared for the holy house:

R.3: I love the house of my God so much that I am also giving my own treasure of gold and silver for it. This is in addition to everything I have already gathered for the holy house.

decisions.choice: treasure: a private, prized possession
decisions.reason: The word means property kept as one's own special treasure, like the treasure of kings in Ecclesiastes 2:8. God uses it of Israel as 'my treasured possession' (Exodus 19:5). David gives from his personal wealth, not only from the stores he had already set aside as king.

decisions.choice: delight: love and pleasure in God's house
decisions.reason: The verb means to take pleasure in or be pleased with. David's gift springs from his love for the house of God (compare Psalm 26:8). The same verb is used of God's pleasure in uprightness in verse 17.

decisions.choice: I love the house of my God so much that
decisions.reason: Readable turns 'in my delight' into a plain statement of why David gives.

records.source: שְׁלֹ֧שֶׁת אֲלָפִ֛ים כִּכְּרֵ֥י זָהָ֖ב מִזְּהַ֣ב אוֹפִ֑יר וְשִׁבְעַ֨ת אֲלָפִ֤ים כִּכַּר־כֶּ֨סֶף֙ מְזֻקָּ֔ק לָט֖וּחַ קִיר֥וֹת הַבָּתִּֽים׃
records.gloss: three thousand talents of gold from [the] gold of Ophir, and seven thousand talents of silver refined for overlaying [the] walls of the houses,
pieces: {{units:about 110 tons|3,000 talents}} of gold, gold of Ophir, and {{units:about 260 tons|7,000 talents}} of refined silver for covering the walls of the buildings,

L.4: 3,000 talents of gold, from the gold of Ophir, and 7,000 talents of refined silver for overlaying the walls of the houses,

R.4: I am giving {{units:about 110 tons|3,000 talents}} of gold from Ophir, the finest gold, and {{units:about 260 tons|7,000 talents}} of pure silver to cover the walls of the buildings.

decisions.choice: Ophir: a distant land famous for its gold
decisions.reason: Solomon's ships later brought gold from Ophir (1 Kings 9:28; 10:11). Its location is unknown; southern Arabia, the east coast of Africa and India have all been suggested. 'Gold of Ophir' was a byword for the finest gold (Job 28:16; Psalm 45:10).

decisions.choice: talents: very large weights
decisions.reason: A talent was about 75 pounds, so these are enormous amounts: Solomon's whole yearly income of gold was 666 talents (1 Kings 10:14). Added to the 100,000 talents of gold already set aside (22:14), the figures present David's gift as beyond counting.

decisions.choice: the houses: the buildings and rooms of the temple
decisions.reason: The plural most likely means the temple's buildings and rooms (28:11), whose walls were to be overlaid with precious metal (2 Chronicles 3:4-9).

decisions.choice: modern weight, with talents as the alternative
decisions.reason: A talent is about 75 pounds, so 3,000 talents is about 225,000 pounds and 7,000 about 525,000 pounds; the round figures in tons are easier to take in.

decisions.choice: from Ophir, the finest gold
decisions.reason: Readable adds what 'gold of Ophir' meant to the first hearers.

records.source: לַזָּהָ֤ב לַזָּהָב֙ וְלַכֶּ֣סֶף לַכֶּ֔סֶף וּלְכָל־מְלָאכָ֖ה בְּיַ֣ד חָרָשִׁ֑ים וּמִ֣י מִתְנַדֵּ֔ב לְמַלֹּ֥אות יָד֛וֹ הַיּ֖וֹם לַיהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: the gold for the gold, and the silver for the silver, and for all [the] work by [the] hand of craftsmen. And who [is] offering willingly to fill his hand today for Yahweh?
pieces: gold for the things of gold and silver for the things of silver, and for all the work to be done by craftsmen. Now who is willing to give freely and consecrate {{gender:themselves|himself}} today to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}?"

L.5: the gold for the [things of] gold, and the silver for the [things of] silver, and for all the work by the hand of craftsmen. And who [is] offering willingly to fill his hand today for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}?"

R.5: The gold and silver are for all the gold and silver objects and for all the work the skilled workers will do. Now, who else will gladly bring a gift today and so dedicate {{gender:themselves|himself}} to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}?"

decisions.choice: fill his hand: consecrate himself by bringing a gift
alternatives: fill his hand with a gift
decisions.reason: To 'fill the hand' is the phrase used for installing priests in their office (Exodus 28:41; 29:9). Here David invites the assembly to set themselves apart for Yahweh, and the next verses show that they did so by giving. The picture of hands filled with gifts may also be in view.

decisions.choice: offering willingly: giving freely, of one's own accord
decisions.reason: The verb is used of freewill gifts and of volunteering (Exodus 35:29; Judges 5:2, 9). It runs through this chapter (verses 6, 9, 14, 17): the gifts were not a tax but given gladly.

decisions.choice: themselves / himself
decisions.reason: David's question is open to the whole assembly, so the inclusive pronoun is the default.

decisions.choice: who else will gladly bring a gift
decisions.reason: David has just told of his own gift, so Readable adds 'else' and spells out the sense of giving freely.

records.source: וַיִּֽתְנַדְּבוּ֩ שָׂרֵ֨י הָאָב֜וֹת וְשָׂרֵ֣י׀שִׁבְטֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וְשָׂרֵ֤י הָאֲלָפִים֙ וְהַמֵּא֔וֹת וּלְשָׂרֵ֖י מְלֶ֥אכֶת הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃
records.gloss: And offered willingly [the] princes of the fathers and [the] princes of [the] tribes of Israel and [the] commanders of the thousands and the hundreds, and the princes of [the] work of the king.
pieces: Then the family leaders and the tribal leaders of Israel gave freely, together with the commanders over thousands and hundreds and the officials who managed the king's work.

L.6: And the princes of the fathers' [houses] and the princes of the tribes of Israel and the commanders of the thousands and the hundreds and the princes over the work of the king offered willingly.

R.6: Then the leaders of the families and of the tribes of Israel, the army commanders over thousands and over hundreds, and the officials in charge of the king's work all gladly gave gifts.

decisions.choice: princes of the fathers: heads of the family groups
decisions.reason: 'The fathers' is short for 'the fathers' houses', the extended families (24:4; 27:1). Their heads stand first among the givers.

decisions.choice: commanders of thousands and hundreds: the army's officers
decisions.reason: The army was organized in units of thousands and hundreds (27:1; 28:1).

decisions.choice: offered willingly: as Israel gave for the tabernacle
decisions.reason: As the people once gave freely for the tabernacle (Exodus 35:21-29), so the leaders now give freely for the temple.

decisions.choice: leaders / commanders / officials
decisions.reason: The word is 'princes' at Literal. Balanced and Readable say 'leaders' for the heads of families and tribes and 'officials' for those over the king's work, which suits each office; the army officers are 'commanders' at every level.

records.source: וַֽיִּתְּנ֞וּ לַעֲבוֹדַ֣ת בֵּית־הָאֱלֹהִ֗ים זָהָ֞ב כִּכָּרִ֣ים חֲמֵֽשֶׁת־אֲלָפִים֮ וַאֲדַרְכֹנִ֣ים רִבּוֹ֒ וְכֶ֗סֶף כִּכָּרִים֙ עֲשֶׂ֣רֶת אֲלָפִ֔ים וּנְחֹ֕שֶׁת רִבּ֛וֹ וּשְׁמוֹנַ֥ת אֲלָפִ֖ים כִּכָּרִ֑ים וּבַרְזֶ֖ל מֵֽאָה־אֶ֥לֶף כִּכָּרִֽים׃
records.gloss: And they gave for [the] service of [the] house of God gold, talents five thousand and darics ten thousand, and silver, talents ten thousand, and bronze, ten thousand and eight thousand talents, and iron, one hundred thousand talents.
pieces: For the service of the house of God they gave {{units:about 190 tons|5,000 talents}} and {{units:about 185 pounds|10,000 darics}} of gold, {{units:about 375 tons|10,000 talents}} of silver, {{units:about 675 tons|18,000 talents}} of bronze and {{units:about 3,750 tons|100,000 talents}} of iron.

L.7: And they gave for the service of the house of God: gold, 5,000 talents and 10,000 darics; and silver, 10,000 talents; and bronze, 18,000 talents; and iron, 100,000 talents.

R.7: They gave all this for the work on God's house: {{units:about 190 tons|5,000 talents}} of gold, and {{units:about 185 pounds|10,000 darics}} more in gold coins, {{units:about 375 tons|10,000 talents}} of silver, {{units:about 675 tons|18,000 talents}} of bronze and {{units:about 3,750 tons|100,000 talents}} of iron.

decisions.choice: darics: Persian gold coins
decisions.reason: The daric was a gold coin first struck under the Persian king Darius I, about five hundred years after David, weighing a little under a third of an ounce. There were no coins in David's day, so the writer of Chronicles, who lived in the Persian period, states part of the gift in the money his own readers used. Some take the word instead as the Greek drachma (a related word appears in Ezra 2:69 and Nehemiah 7:69).

decisions.choice: the service of the house of God: the work of building and furnishing it
decisions.reason: Here 'service' means the work on the temple, as in 28:13-14, 20, not only the worship later carried on in it.

decisions.choice: talents: as in verse 4
decisions.reason: As in verse 4, the figures are immense; the iron alone would weigh about 3,750 tons. The bronze is counted in Hebrew as 'ten thousand and eight thousand' talents.

decisions.choice: modern weight, with talents and darics as the alternative
decisions.reason: A talent is about 75 pounds. A daric weighed about 8.4 grams, so 10,000 darics is about 185 pounds of gold. Readable adds 'in gold coins' so the reader knows a daric is a coin.

records.source: וְהַנִּמְצָ֤א אִתּוֹ֙ אֲבָנִ֔ים נָתְנ֖וּ לְאוֹצַ֣ר בֵּית־יְהוָ֑ה עַ֥ל יַד־יְחִיאֵ֖ל הַגֵּרְשֻׁנִּֽי׃
records.gloss: And the [one] found with him stones gave [them] to [the] treasury of [the] house of Yahweh, into [the] hand of Jehiel the Gershonite.
pieces: Any who owned precious stones handed them over to the treasury of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, in the care of Jehiel the Gershonite.

L.8: And whoever had stones found with him gave [them] to the treasury of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, into the hand of Jehiel the Gershonite.

R.8: Those who had jewels gave them to the treasury of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Jehiel, from the Levite clan of Gershon, took charge of them.

decisions.choice: stones: precious stones
decisions.reason: After the precious stones of verse 2, 'stones' here means gems.

decisions.choice: into the hand of Jehiel: in his care
decisions.reason: Jehiel the Gershonite, a Levite, was in charge of the temple treasuries (23:8; 26:21-22).

decisions.choice: from the Levite clan of Gershon
decisions.reason: Readable explains the clan name.

records.source: וַיִּשְׂמְח֤וּ הָעָם֙ עַל־הִֽתְנַדְּבָ֔ם כִּ֚י בְּלֵ֣ב שָׁלֵ֔ם הִֽתְנַדְּב֖וּ לַיהוָ֑ה וְגַם֙ דָּוִ֣יד הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ שָׂמַ֖ח שִׂמְחָ֥ה גְדוֹלָֽה׃פ
records.gloss: And rejoiced the people over their offering willingly, for with a heart whole they offered willingly to Yahweh; and also David the king rejoiced [with] joy great.
pieces: The people rejoiced over these freewill gifts, for with a whole heart they had given freely to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. King David also rejoiced with great joy.

L.9: And the people rejoiced over their offering willingly, for with a whole heart they offered willingly to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; and David the king also rejoiced [with] great joy.

R.9: The people were very happy about these gifts, because they had been given freely and with all their heart to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. King David was also full of joy.

decisions.choice: their offering: the giving of the leaders, or of all who gave
decisions.reason: 'They' may be the leaders of verse 6, whose generosity made the people glad, or the people themselves, glad at their own giving. The verse does not say, and the wording keeps both open.

decisions.choice: with a whole heart: with undivided, sincere devotion
decisions.reason: A 'whole heart' is undivided loyalty (28:9; 1 Kings 8:61). David prays for the same heart for Solomon in verse 19.

decisions.choice: with all their heart
decisions.reason: Readable uses the familiar phrase for 'a whole heart'.

records.source: וַיְבָ֤רֶךְ דָּוִיד֙ אֶת־יְהוָ֔ה לְעֵינֵ֖י כָּל־הַקָּהָ֑ל וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִ֗יד בָּר֨וּךְ אַתָּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵי֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל אָבִ֔ינוּ מֵעוֹלָ֖ם וְעַד־עוֹלָֽם׃
records.gloss: And blessed David Yahweh before [the] eyes of all the assembly, and said David, Blessed [are] you, Yahweh, God of Israel our father, from everlasting and to everlasting.
pieces: Then David blessed {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in the sight of the whole assembly. David said, "Blessed are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, God of our father Israel, from everlasting to everlasting.

L.10: And David blessed {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} before the eyes of all the assembly, and David said, "Blessed [are] {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, God of Israel our father, from everlasting and to everlasting.

R.10: Then David praised {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in front of all the people gathered there. He said, "Praise be to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, God of our ancestor Israel, for ever and ever.

decisions.choice: blessed: praised with thanks
decisions.reason: When people 'bless' God they praise and thank God; they do not give God something lacking. The same verb is used of the assembly in verse 20.

decisions.choice: Israel our father: Jacob
decisions.reason: Israel here is the patriarch Jacob, whose name God changed to Israel (Genesis 32:29), the ancestor of the whole people. Verse 18 names him with Abraham and Isaac.

decisions.choice: from everlasting to everlasting: for all time, past and future
decisions.reason: The same phrase closes the psalm of 16:36 (Psalm 106:48) and describes God in Psalm 90:2.

decisions.choice: Praise be to you
decisions.reason: Readable says in plain words what 'blessed' means when it is said of God.

records.heading: David's prayer of praise

records.source: לְךָ֣ יְ֠הוָה הַגְּדֻלָּ֨ה וְהַגְּבוּרָ֤ה וְהַתִּפְאֶ֨רֶת֙ וְהַנֵּ֣צַח וְהַה֔וֹד כִּי־כֹ֖ל בַּשָּׁמַ֣יִם וּבָאָ֑רֶץ לְךָ֤ יְהוָה֙ הַמַּמְלָכָ֔ה וְהַמִּתְנַשֵּׂ֖א לְכֹ֥ל׀לְרֹֽאשׁ׃
records.gloss: To you, Yahweh, [are] the greatness and the might and the splendor and the victory and the majesty, for all in the heavens and on the earth [is yours]; to you, Yahweh, [is] the kingdom, and the [one] lifting himself up over all as head.
pieces: To {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, belong the greatness, the power, the glory, the victory and the majesty; indeed everything in heaven and on earth is {{deity_pronoun:yours|Yours}}. The kingdom is {{deity_pronoun:yours|Yours}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are lifted high as head over all.

L.11: Yours, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, [are] the greatness and the power and the glory and the victory and the majesty, for all [that is] in the heavens and on the earth [is {{deity_pronoun:yours|Yours}}]; {{deity_pronoun:yours|Yours}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, [is] the kingdom, and [{{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are] the one exalted over all as head.

R.11: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are great and powerful. Glory, victory and majesty belong to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. Everything in heaven and on earth is {{deity_pronoun:yours|Yours}}. The kingdom is {{deity_pronoun:yours|Yours}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}. You are lifted high as the ruler over everything.

decisions.choice: a doxology: praise of God's greatness
decisions.reason: Verses 10-13 are a doxology, a formal hymn of praise, with balanced lists like those of the psalms. The Hebrew text sets them as part of David's spoken prayer within the story, and they are laid out here as prose, like the rest of the prayer.

decisions.choice: victory
decisions.reason: The word can mean preeminence or lastingness (in 1 Samuel 15:29 God is 'the Glory' or 'the Eternal One' of Israel), and in later Hebrew it means victory. In a list of royal attributes victory fits best, but lasting glory is possible.

decisions.choice: glory: splendor, beauty
decisions.reason: The word means beauty or splendor that draws honor, here the splendor of a king; it is not the usual word for glory, which verse 12 uses for 'honor'. It comes again in verse 13.

decisions.choice: echoed in the closing praise of the Lord's Prayer in some manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts of Matthew add to the Lord's Prayer, 'for yours is the kingdom and the power and the glory forever' (Matthew 6:13). That closing praise, which is not in the earliest manuscripts, seems to be modelled on David's words here, which call the kingdom, the power and the glory God's. The link is likely but cannot be proved.

decisions.choice: To you belong ... / The kingdom is yours
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable keep the order of the list but put the two 'Yours, LORD' clauses in natural English order.

records.source: וְהָעֹ֤שֶׁר וְהַכָּבוֹד֙ מִלְּפָנֶ֔יךָ וְאַתָּה֙ מוֹשֵׁ֣ל בַּכֹּ֔ל וּבְיָדְךָ֖ כֹּ֣חַ וּגְבוּרָ֑ה וּבְיָ֣דְךָ֔ לְגַדֵּ֥ל וּלְחַזֵּ֖ק לַכֹּֽל׃
records.gloss: And the riches and the honor [are] from before you, and you [are] ruling over all, and in your hand [are] power and might, and in your hand [it is] to make great and to strengthen all.
pieces: Riches and honor come from {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} rule over everything. In {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hand are power and might, and it is in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hand to make anyone great and to give strength to all.

L.12: And the riches and the honor [are] from before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} [are] ruling over all, and in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hand [are] power and might, and in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hand [it is] to make great and to give strength to all.

R.12: Wealth and honor come from {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. You rule over everything. You have power and strength, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} can make anyone great and strong.

decisions.choice: honor: standing and respect
decisions.reason: The word is the usual word for glory; paired with riches it means the standing and respect God gives to people. Verse 28 says David died full of riches and honor (compare 1 Kings 3:13).

decisions.choice: in your hand: in your power
decisions.reason: The hand stands for power and control. Greatness and strength are God's to give.

decisions.choice: to make anyone great
decisions.reason: 'To make great' has no object in the Hebrew; 'all' at the end belongs to both verbs, so Balanced and Readable say 'anyone'.

records.source: וְעַתָּ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ מוֹדִ֥ים אֲנַ֖חְנוּ לָ֑ךְ וּֽמְהַֽלְלִ֖ים לְשֵׁ֥ם תִּפְאַרְתֶּֽךָ׃
records.gloss: And now, our God, giving thanks we [are] to you, and praising [the] name of your splendor.
pieces: And now, our God, we give {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} thanks and praise {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} glorious name.

L.13: And now, our God, we [are] giving thanks to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} and praising the name of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} splendor.

R.13: Now, our God, we thank {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, and we praise {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} wonderful name.

decisions.choice: the name of your splendor: your glorious name
decisions.reason: Hebrew often uses 'of' with a noun where other languages use an adjective. 'Splendor' is the word of verse 11. God's name stands for God as made known to people (Exodus 34:5-7).

decisions.choice: wonderful
decisions.reason: Readable uses a common word for 'glorious'.

records.source: וְכִ֨י מִ֤י אֲנִי֙ וּמִ֣י עַמִּ֔י כִּֽי־נַעְצֹ֣ר כֹּ֔חַ לְהִתְנַדֵּ֖ב כָּזֹ֑את כִּֽי־מִמְּךָ֣ הַכֹּ֔ל וּמִיָּדְךָ֖ נָתַ֥נּוּ לָֽךְ׃
records.gloss: And indeed who [am] I and who [are] my people, that we should retain strength to offer willingly like this? For from you [is] everything, and from your hand we have given to you.
pieces: But who am I, and who are my people, that we should have the means to give as freely as this? Everything comes from {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; what we have given {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} came from {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} own hand.

L.14: But who [am] I, and who [are] my people, that we should retain strength to offer willingly like this? For everything [is] from {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, and from {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hand we have given to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

R.14: But who am I, and who are my people? How could we ever give so much? Everything comes from {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. We have only given back to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} gave us.

decisions.choice: retain strength: be able
decisions.reason: To 'retain strength' means to have the means or the ability to do something (2 Chronicles 2:5; 13:20).

decisions.choice: who am I: David's humble question
decisions.reason: David asked the same when God promised him a lasting house (17:16; 2 Samuel 7:18).

decisions.choice: everything is from God: the gift returns what God first gave
decisions.reason: David's humility rests on the belief that all wealth is God's gift (Deuteronomy 8:17-18). The givers only hand back what came from God.

decisions.choice: who am I ...? How could we ever give so much?
decisions.reason: Readable splits the long question in two.

records.source: כִּֽי־גֵרִ֨ים אֲנַ֧חְנוּ לְפָנֶ֛יךָ וְתוֹשָׁבִ֖ים כְּכָל־אֲבֹתֵ֑ינוּ כַּצֵּ֧ל׀יָמֵ֛ינוּ עַל־הָאָ֖רֶץ וְאֵ֥ין מִקְוֶֽה׃
records.gloss: For sojourners we [are] before you, and settlers, like all our fathers; like the shadow [are] our days on the earth, and there is no hope.
pieces: For we are outsiders before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, and temporary settlers, as all our ancestors were. Our days on earth are like a shadow, with no hope of staying.

L.15: For we [are] sojourners before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, and settlers, like all our fathers; like a shadow [are] our days on the earth, and there is no hope.

R.15: We are like strangers and visitors in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} presence, as all our ancestors were. Our days on earth pass like a shadow, and they do not last.

decisions.choice: sojourners and settlers: people living on land that is not their own
decisions.reason: A sojourner lives among a people not his own, without the rights of birth; a settler is a resident with no land of his own. God says the same of Israel in the land: 'you are sojourners and settlers with me' (Leviticus 25:23), and Abraham called himself both in Canaan (Genesis 23:4). David confesses that even as king, in the land God gave, he and his people hold nothing by right.

decisions.choice: Psalm 39:13 and Job 8:9
decisions.reason: A psalm of David says, 'I am a sojourner with you, a settler, like all my fathers' (Psalm 39:13), and Job 8:9 says, 'our days on the earth are a shadow' (compare Psalm 144:4).

decisions.choice: no hope: nothing lasting to count on
decisions.reason: The word usually means hope or expectation (Ezra 10:2; Jeremiah 14:8). After the picture of a passing shadow, it means there is nothing lasting to rely on: life on earth does not stay. Some read it as 'no abiding', no permanence.

decisions.choice: sojourners and settlers / outsiders and temporary settlers / strangers and visitors
decisions.reason: The word for sojourner follows the wording used since Leviticus at each level; 'settlers' is made 'temporary settlers' and 'visitors' to show they are not owners.

decisions.choice: with no hope of staying / they do not last
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable spell out what the bare 'no hope' means after the picture of the shadow.

records.source: יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ כֹ֣ל הֶהָמ֤וֹן הַזֶּה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הֲכִינֹ֔נוּ לִבְנֽוֹת־לְךָ֥ בַ֖יִת לְשֵׁ֣ם קָדְשֶׁ֑ךָ מִיָּדְךָ֥ ה֖וּא וּלְךָ֥ הַכֹּֽל׃
records.gloss: Yahweh our God, all this abundance that we have prepared to build for you a house for [the] name of your holiness, from your hand it [is], and to you [belongs] all.
pieces: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} our God, all this wealth that we have gathered to build a house for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} holy name has come from {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hand, and every part of it belongs to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

L.16: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} our God, all this abundance that we have prepared to build {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} a house for the name of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} holiness, from {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hand it [is], and all [is] {{deity_pronoun:yours|Yours}}.

R.16: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} our God, we have gathered all these riches to build a house to honor {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} holy name. But all of it came from {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, and all of it is {{deity_pronoun:yours|Yours}}.

decisions.choice: abundance: a great quantity
decisions.reason: The word means a crowd or a great mass; here the great heap of gifts.

decisions.choice: a house for your holy name
decisions.reason: The temple is called a house 'for the name' of God (22:7-10; 2 Samuel 7:13; 1 Kings 8:29). God is not contained in it (2 Chronicles 6:18) but chooses to be known and called on there.

decisions.choice: to honor your holy name
decisions.reason: Readable explains what it means to build a house 'for' God's name.

records.source: וְיָדַ֣עְתִּי אֱלֹהַ֔י כִּ֤י אַתָּה֙ בֹּחֵ֣ן לֵבָ֔ב וּמֵישָׁרִ֖ים תִּרְצֶ֑ה אֲנִ֗י בְּיֹ֤שֶׁר לְבָבִי֙ הִתְנַדַּ֣בְתִּי כָל־אֵ֔לֶּה וְעַתָּ֗ה עַמְּךָ֙ הַנִּמְצְאוּ־פֹ֔ה רָאִ֥יתִי בְשִׂמְחָ֖ה לְהִֽתְנַדֶּב־לָֽךְ׃
records.gloss: And I know, my God, that you [are] testing [the] heart, and uprightness you take pleasure in; I, in [the] uprightness of my heart I have offered willingly all these, and now your people found here I have seen with joy offering willingly to you.
pieces: My God, I know that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} examine the heart and that uprightness pleases {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. With an upright heart I have freely given all these things, and now I have watched {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people gathered here give freely to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} with joy.

L.17: And I know, my God, that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} [are] testing the heart and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} take pleasure in uprightness. As for me, in the uprightness of my heart I have offered willingly all these [things]; and now I have seen {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people who are found here offering willingly to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} with joy.

R.17: My God, I know that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} look into people's hearts and that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are pleased when they are honest. I have given all these things freely and with an honest heart. And now I have seen {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people here giving to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} freely and with joy.

decisions.choice: test the heart: examine the inner motives
decisions.reason: God weighs the motives behind a gift, not only the gift (28:9; Psalm 7:10; Jeremiah 11:20). David speaks of his upright heart before the one who knows it.

decisions.choice: uprightness: straightness of motive, sincerity
decisions.reason: Both words come from a root meaning straight or level. Here they mean giving with no hidden motive.

decisions.choice: with joy: the people's joy, or David's
decisions.reason: The phrase may say that the people gave with joy, or that David watched them with joy. Both are true in the story (verse 9), and the wording keeps both open.

decisions.choice: look into people's hearts / pleased when they are honest
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom of testing the heart and uses 'honest' for uprightness.

records.source: יְהוָ֗ה אֱ֠לֹהֵי אַבְרָהָ֞ם יִצְחָ֤ק וְיִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֲבֹתֵ֔ינוּ שֳׁמְרָה־זֹּ֣את לְעוֹלָ֔ם לְיֵ֥צֶר מַחְשְׁב֖וֹת לְבַ֣ב עַמֶּ֑ךָ וְהָכֵ֥ן לְבָבָ֖ם אֵלֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: Yahweh, God of Abraham, Isaac and Israel our fathers, keep this forever for [the] inclination of [the] thoughts of [the] heart of your people, and direct their heart to you.
pieces: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, God of our ancestors Abraham, Isaac and Israel, keep this willingness forever in the purposes and thoughts of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people's hearts, and set their hearts firmly on {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

L.18: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, God of Abraham, Isaac and Israel our fathers, keep this forever as the inclination of the thoughts of the heart of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people, and direct their heart to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

R.18: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, God of our ancestors Abraham, Isaac and Israel, help {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people always want to give like this. Keep their hearts loyal to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

decisions.choice: keep this: preserve this willingness
decisions.reason: 'This' points back to the people's glad giving (verse 17). David asks God to keep it alive in them for all time.

decisions.choice: the inclination of the thoughts of the heart
decisions.reason: The same words describe the human heart's bent toward evil before the flood (Genesis 6:5), and in 28:9 God understands 'every inclination of the thoughts'. David prays that the bent of the people's hearts will stay turned toward God.

decisions.choice: direct their heart: make their heart firm and steady
decisions.reason: The verb means to make firm or set in place; with 'heart' it means to fix one's loyalty steadily (1 Samuel 7:3; 2 Chronicles 30:19).

decisions.choice: Israel: Jacob
decisions.reason: As in verse 10.

decisions.choice: this willingness / always want to give like this
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name what 'this' refers to.

records.source: וְלִשְׁלֹמֹ֣ה בְנִ֗י תֵּ֚ן לֵבָ֣ב שָׁלֵ֔ם לִשְׁמוֹר֙ מִצְוֺתֶ֔יךָ עֵדְוֺתֶ֖יךָ וְחֻקֶּ֑יךָ וְלַעֲשׂ֣וֹת הַכֹּ֔ל וְלִבְנ֖וֹת הַבִּירָ֥ה אֲשֶׁר־הֲכִינֽוֹתִי׃פ
records.gloss: And to Solomon my son give a heart whole to keep your commandments, your testimonies and your statutes, and to do all, and to build the palace [for] which I have prepared.
pieces: Give my son Solomon a whole heart to keep {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commandments, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} decrees and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} statutes, to carry them all out, and to build the palace for which I have made preparations."

L.19: And to Solomon my son give a whole heart to keep {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commandments, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} testimonies and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} statutes, and to do all [of them], and to build the palace for which I have made provision."

R.19: And give my son Solomon a heart that is completely loyal, so that he will obey {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commands, instructions and laws and do everything they say. Help him build the palace for which I have gathered all these things."

decisions.choice: a whole heart: undivided loyalty
decisions.reason: As in verse 9; compare 28:9 and 1 Kings 8:61, and the later verdict on Solomon's heart in 1 Kings 11:4.

decisions.choice: to do all: to carry out all the commandments
decisions.reason: 'All' most naturally refers to the commandments just named. It could also mean all the work needed, but the next phrase names the building separately.

decisions.choice: palace
decisions.reason: As in verse 1.

decisions.choice: commandments, testimonies, statutes / commandments, decrees, statutes / commands, instructions, laws
decisions.reason: The three words for God's law keep the wording used since Exodus and Deuteronomy at each level.

decisions.choice: Help him build
decisions.reason: Readable makes a new sentence of the last request.

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר דָּוִיד֙ לְכָל־הַקָּהָ֔ל בָּֽרְכוּ־נָ֖א אֶת־יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֑ם וַיְבָרֲכ֣וּ כָֽל־הַקָּהָ֗ל לַיהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י אֲבֹֽתֵיהֶ֔ם וַיִּקְּד֧וּ וַיִּֽשְׁתַּחֲו֛וּ לַיהוָ֖ה וְלַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃
records.gloss: And said David to all the assembly, Bless please Yahweh your God; and blessed all the assembly Yahweh, God of their fathers, and they bowed and prostrated themselves to Yahweh and to the king.
pieces: Then David said to the whole assembly, "Now bless {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God." And the whole assembly blessed {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of their ancestors. They bowed their heads and lay face down before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and before the king.

L.20: And David said to all the assembly, "Bless now {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God." And all the assembly blessed {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of their fathers, and they bowed and prostrated themselves to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and to the king.

R.20: Then David said to all the people, "Now praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God." So all the people praised {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of their ancestors. They bowed low and knelt with their faces to the ground to worship {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and to honor the king.

decisions.choice: bowed to Yahweh and to the king: worship and homage
decisions.reason: The same gestures express worship of God and respect for a king (1 Samuel 24:9; 1 Kings 1:16, 31). Placed together here, they give worship to Yahweh and honor to the king whom Yahweh had placed on the throne.

decisions.choice: bowed: bowed the head
decisions.reason: The first verb means to bow the head; the second, to lie face down on the ground (Genesis 24:26; Exodus 4:31).

decisions.choice: to worship the LORD and to honor the king
decisions.reason: Readable says what the one gesture meant toward each.

records.heading: Solomon is made king

records.source: וַיִּזְבְּח֣וּ לַיהוָ֣ה׀זְ֠בָחִים וַיַּעֲל֨וּ עֹל֜וֹת לַיהוָ֗ה לְֽמָחֳרַת֮ הַיּ֣וֹם הַהוּא֒ פָּרִ֨ים אֶ֜לֶף אֵילִ֥ים אֶ֛לֶף כְּבָשִׂ֥ים אֶ֖לֶף וְנִסְכֵּיהֶ֑ם וּזְבָחִ֥ים לָרֹ֖ב לְכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And they sacrificed to Yahweh sacrifices, and they offered up burnt offerings to Yahweh on [the] morrow of that day: bulls a thousand, rams a thousand, lambs a thousand, and their drink offerings, and sacrifices in abundance for all Israel.
pieces: The next day they offered sacrifices to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and burnt offerings to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: 1,000 bulls, 1,000 rams and 1,000 lambs, each with its drink offering, and a great many sacrifices for all Israel.

L.21: And they sacrificed sacrifices to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and offered up burnt offerings to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} on the morrow of that day: 1,000 bulls, 1,000 rams, 1,000 lambs, and their drink offerings, and sacrifices in abundance for all Israel.

R.21: The next day they made sacrifices to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and gave {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} burnt offerings: 1,000 young bulls, 1,000 rams and 1,000 lambs. They also gave the drink offerings that went with them, and many other sacrifices for all the people of Israel.

decisions.choice: sacrifices: offerings shared in a meal
decisions.reason: Set beside burnt offerings, which were burned whole, these are sacrifices whose meat the worshipers ate (Leviticus 7:15; Deuteronomy 12:27). This explains the feast of verse 22.

decisions.choice: drink offerings: wine poured out with each animal
decisions.reason: Wine was poured out with each burnt offering, in a set amount for each kind of animal (Numbers 15:1-10).

decisions.choice: on the morrow of that day: the next day
decisions.reason: The day after the gathering of verses 1-20.

decisions.choice: young bulls
decisions.reason: The word names young bulls, the usual animal for a large burnt offering.

records.source: וַיֹּאכְל֨וּ וַיִּשְׁתּ֜וּ לִפְנֵ֧י יְהוָ֛ה בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא בְּשִׂמְחָ֣ה גְדוֹלָ֑ה וַיַּמְלִ֤יכוּ שֵׁנִית֙ לִשְׁלֹמֹ֣ה בֶן־דָּוִ֔יד וַיִּמְשְׁח֧וּ לַיהוָ֛ה לְנָגִ֥יד וּלְצָד֖וֹק לְכֹהֵֽן׃
records.gloss: And they ate and drank before Yahweh on that day with joy great, and they made king a second [time] Solomon son of David, and they anointed [him] for Yahweh as ruler, and Zadok as priest.
pieces: They ate and drank before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} that day with great joy. Then they made Solomon son of David king a second time and anointed him as ruler for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and Zadok as priest.

L.22: And they ate and drank before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} on that day with great joy. And they made Solomon son of David king a second [time], and they anointed [him] for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as ruler, and Zadok as priest.

R.22: That day they ate and drank in the presence of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with great joy. Then they made David's son Solomon king a second time. They anointed him to be the leader who would serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and they anointed Zadok to be priest.

decisions.choice: a second time: a public confirmation
decisions.reason: The first time is told briefly in 23:1 ('David made Solomon his son king over Israel') and fully in 1 Kings 1:32-40, where Zadok anointed Solomon in haste when Adonijah tried to take the throne. Now the whole assembly confirms him publicly.

decisions.choice: ruler: the leader appointed by Yahweh
decisions.reason: The title is used of kings as chosen and appointed by Yahweh (1 Samuel 9:16; 2 Samuel 7:8; 1 Chronicles 28:4).

decisions.choice: Zadok as priest: chief priest of the new reign
decisions.reason: Zadok was already serving as a priest (16:39; 24:3). His anointing marks him as chief priest under Solomon, who later removed Abiathar and put Zadok in his place (1 Kings 2:35).

decisions.choice: the leader who would serve the LORD
decisions.reason: Readable explains that he was anointed 'for' the LORD, as the LORD's appointed ruler.

records.source: וַיֵּ֣שֶׁב שְׁ֠לֹמֹה עַל־כִּסֵּ֨א יְהוָ֧ה׀לְמֶ֛לֶךְ תַּֽחַת־דָּוִ֥יד אָבִ֖יו וַיַּצְלַ֑ח וַיִּשְׁמְע֥וּ אֵלָ֖יו כָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And sat Solomon on [the] throne of Yahweh as king in place of David his father, and he prospered, and listened to him all Israel.
pieces: So Solomon took his seat on the throne of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as king, succeeding his father David. He prospered, and all Israel obeyed him.

L.23: And Solomon sat on the throne of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as king in place of David his father, and he prospered, and all Israel listened to him.

R.23: Solomon sat on the throne of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and ruled as king in place of his father David. He was successful, and all the people of Israel obeyed him.

decisions.choice: the throne of Yahweh: the king rules on God's behalf
decisions.reason: Chronicles speaks of Israel's throne as Yahweh's own (28:5, 'the throne of the kingdom of Yahweh over Israel'; 17:14; 2 Chronicles 9:8). The king of David's line sits on it as Yahweh's representative; the true king is Yahweh.

decisions.choice: compare 1 Kings 2:12
decisions.reason: Kings says Solomon 'sat on the throne of David his father'. Chronicles calls the same throne Yahweh's.

decisions.choice: listened to: obeyed
decisions.reason: To listen to a king is to obey him.

records.source: וְכָל־הַשָּׂרִים֙ וְהַגִּבֹּרִ֔ים וְגַ֕ם כָּל־בְּנֵ֖י הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ דָּוִ֑יד נָ֣תְנוּ יָ֔ד תַּ֖חַת שְׁלֹמֹ֥ה הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃
records.gloss: And all the princes and the mighty men and also all [the] sons of the king David gave a hand under Solomon the king.
pieces: All the officials and the mighty warriors, and also all King David's sons, pledged their loyalty to King Solomon.

L.24: And all the princes and the mighty men, and also all the sons of King David, gave a hand under Solomon the king.

R.24: All the leaders and the best warriors, and all of King David's other sons too, promised to be loyal to King Solomon.

decisions.choice: gave a hand under: pledged allegiance
decisions.reason: To give the hand is to make a pledge (2 Kings 10:15; Ezra 10:19); 'under' marks submission. The leaders swore loyalty to the new king.

decisions.choice: all the sons of King David: even his rivals
decisions.reason: Even David's other sons, one of whom, Adonijah, had tried to take the throne (1 Kings 1:5-10), submitted to Solomon.

decisions.choice: officials / leaders; mighty warriors / best warriors
decisions.reason: The word for 'princes' follows the wording used at each level, and the warriors are worded as in 11:10.

decisions.choice: other sons
decisions.reason: Readable adds 'other', since Solomon is himself one of David's sons.

records.source: וַיְגַדֵּ֨ל יְהוָ֤ה אֶת־שְׁלֹמֹה֙ לְמַ֔עְלָה לְעֵינֵ֖י כָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיִּתֵּ֤ן עָלָיו֙ ה֣וֹד מַלְכ֔וּת אֲ֠שֶׁר לֹֽא־הָיָ֧ה עַל־כָּל־מֶ֛לֶךְ לְפָנָ֖יו עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃פ
records.gloss: And made great Yahweh Solomon upward in [the] eyes of all Israel, and he put on him majesty of kingship which had not been on any king before him over Israel.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} made Solomon exceedingly great in the sight of all Israel and gave him royal majesty such as no king over Israel before him had had.

L.25: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made Solomon great upward in the eyes of all Israel, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} put on him royal majesty that had not been on any king before him over Israel.

R.25: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} made Solomon very great in the eyes of all the people of Israel. He gave Solomon the splendor of a king, more than any king of Israel before him.

decisions.choice: royal majesty: the splendor and authority of a king
decisions.reason: The word for majesty is the one used of God in verse 11: God shares a part of that majesty with the king (Psalm 21:6).

decisions.choice: any king before him: Saul and David
decisions.reason: Only Saul and David had reigned over Israel before Solomon. Compare the promise of riches and honor in 1 Kings 3:12-13.

decisions.choice: great upward / exceedingly great
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says 'upward', meaning very high. Literal keeps the word; Balanced says what it means.

records.source: וְדָוִיד֙ בֶּן־יִשָׁ֔י מָלַ֖ךְ עַל־כָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And David son of Jesse reigned over all Israel.
pieces: So David son of Jesse reigned over all Israel.

L.26: And David son of Jesse reigned over all Israel.

R.26: David son of Jesse had been king over all Israel.

decisions.choice: David son of Jesse: the closing summary of his reign
decisions.reason: The summary goes back to David's beginnings as the son of Jesse of Bethlehem (1 Samuel 16:1; 1 Chronicles 10:14-11:3), the shepherd made king of all Israel.

decisions.choice: had been king
decisions.reason: Readable marks this as a look back over David's whole reign.

records.heading: The end of David's reign

records.source: וְהַיָּמִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר מָלַךְ֙ עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אַרְבָּעִ֖ים שָׁנָ֑ה בְּחֶבְר֤וֹן מָלַךְ֙ שֶׁ֣בַע שָׁנִ֔ים וּבִירוּשָׁלִַ֥ם מָלַ֖ךְ שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים וְשָׁלֽוֹשׁ׃
records.gloss: And the days which he reigned over Israel [were] forty years; in Hebron he reigned seven years, and in Jerusalem he reigned thirty and three.
pieces: His reign over Israel lasted forty years: seven of them he reigned in Hebron, and thirty-three in Jerusalem.

L.27: And the days that he reigned over Israel [were] forty years: in Hebron he reigned seven years, and in Jerusalem he reigned thirty-three [years].

R.27: He was king over Israel for forty years. He ruled in Hebron for seven years and in Jerusalem for thirty-three years.

decisions.choice: parallel to 1 Kings 2:11
decisions.reason: The verse repeats 1 Kings 2:11 almost word for word. Kings names David as the subject and repeats 'years' after thirty-three.

decisions.choice: forty years: a round total
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 5:4-5 gives seven years and six months in Hebron and thirty-three years in Jerusalem. The summary rounds the Hebron years. In Hebron David ruled Judah only (2 Samuel 2:4, 11), but the whole is counted as his reign over Israel.

decisions.choice: wording of 1 Kings 2:11
decisions.reason: The wording at each level follows 1 Kings 2:11, where the Hebrew is the same.

records.source: וַיָּ֨מָת֙ בְּשֵׂיבָ֣ה טוֹבָ֔ה שְׂבַ֥ע יָמִ֖ים עֹ֣שֶׁר וְכָב֑וֹד וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֥ה בְנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו׃
records.gloss: And he died in old age good, full of days, riches and honor, and reigned Solomon his son in his place.
pieces: He died at a good old age, having had his fill of days, riches and honor, and his son Solomon became king in his place.

L.28: And he died in a good old age, full of days, riches and honor; and Solomon his son reigned in his place.

R.28: He died at a good old age, after a long life full of riches and honor. Then his son Solomon became king after him.

decisions.choice: a good old age, full of days: like the patriarchs
decisions.reason: The words echo the deaths of Abraham ('in a good old age, old and full', Genesis 25:8) and Isaac ('old and full of days', Genesis 35:29). David's death is told as the peaceful end of a blessed life.

decisions.choice: compare 1 Kings 2:10
decisions.reason: Kings says that David 'lay down with his fathers and was buried in the City of David'. Chronicles leaves out the burial and stresses the fullness of his life; 'riches and honor' recalls verse 12, which says they come from God.

decisions.choice: full of days: having lived a long, satisfying life
decisions.reason: The word 'full' means satisfied: he had lived as long as one could wish.

decisions.choice: became king in his place / became king after him
decisions.reason: The wording follows the formula for a son succeeding his father in Kings (1 Kings 11:43).

records.source: וְדִבְרֵי֙ דָּוִ֣יד הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ הָרִאשֹׁנִ֖ים וְהָאֲחרֹנִ֑ים הִנָּ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל־דִּבְרֵי֙ שְׁמוּאֵ֣ל הָרֹאֶ֔ה וְעַל־דִּבְרֵי֙ נָתָ֣ן הַנָּבִ֔יא וְעַל־דִּבְרֵ֖י גָּ֥ד הַחֹזֶֽה׃
records.gloss: And [the] matters of David the king, the first and the last, see, they [are] written in [the] words of Samuel the seer and in [the] words of Nathan the prophet and in [the] words of Gad the seer,
pieces: The acts of King David, from first to last, are written in the records of Samuel the seer, the records of Nathan the prophet and the records of Gad the seer,

L.29: And the matters of David the king, the first and the last, see, they [are] written in the words of Samuel the seer, and in the words of Nathan the prophet, and in the words of Gad the seer,

R.29: Everything King David did, from beginning to end, is written down in the records of Samuel the seer, Nathan the prophet and Gad the seer.

decisions.choice: matters / words: David's acts, and the prophets' records of them
decisions.reason: The same word means both 'words' and 'matters, events'. David's 'matters' are his deeds; the 'words' of Samuel, Nathan and Gad are their written accounts. Chronicles often names prophets as the writers of a king's history (2 Chronicles 9:29). These may be the books of Samuel or writings now lost.

decisions.choice: seer: two words for one office
decisions.reason: Samuel is called by one word for seer and Gad by another; both come from verbs of seeing and name a prophet who receives visions. 1 Samuel 9:9 explains that a prophet was once called a seer, using Samuel's word. The two words stand side by side here with no clear difference in meaning.

decisions.choice: the first and the last: the whole story, from beginning to end
decisions.reason: The pair covers everything David did.

decisions.choice: see, they are written / are written
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the pointing word; Balanced and Readable make a plain statement, as with the source formula in Kings.

decisions.choice: a new sentence at verse 30
decisions.reason: Readable ends the sentence here and begins verse 30 as a sentence of its own.

records.source: עִ֥ם כָּל־מַלְכוּת֖וֹ וּגְבוּרָת֑וֹ וְהָעִתִּ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָבְר֤וּ עָלָיו֙ וְעַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְעַ֖ל כָּל־מַמְלְכ֥וֹת הָאֲרָצֽוֹת׃פ
records.gloss: with all his kingship and his might and the times which passed over him and over Israel and over all [the] kingdoms of the lands.
pieces: together with all his reign and his power, and the events that came upon him, upon Israel and upon all the kingdoms of the lands.

L.30: with all his reign and his might, and the times that passed over him and over Israel and over all the kingdoms of the lands.

R.30: They tell about his whole reign and his power, and about all that happened to him, to Israel and to all the kingdoms of the other lands.

decisions.choice: the times that passed over him: the events of his life
decisions.reason: 'Times' means what happened in one's life, good and bad (Psalm 31:16, 'my times are in your hand').

decisions.choice: all the kingdoms of the lands: the nations around Israel
decisions.reason: David's wars and treaties touched the surrounding kingdoms (chapters 18-20).

decisions.choice: They tell about
decisions.reason: Readable begins a new sentence and supplies a verb.
